applied.problem: pV = C is the isothermal case only for an ideal gas (the cited source states it after PV = mRT); for a real working fluid such as wet steam a constant-temperature expansion is not pV = C, so the bare claim overreaches.
Not every constant-course track spirals towards the pole: a course due east or west follows a parallel and one due north or south follows a meridian, so the general claim needs narrowing.

"Any other law stays curved" is false: with only x logged (a switch this interactive offers) y = a + b log x comes out straight, and along the equator or a meridian the shortest route is a constant-course track.

The worked example reads its gradient from two readings, which contradicts the step just above (read it from two points on the line, not two readings); it should say the best-fit line passes through those points.
